text:
For this activity, you will need:

A paragraph to read. You can choose something from a book you have, or you can use this extract from Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland.
We chose this piece because one character is talking all the way through, which means you can pretend you are an actor in a play (if you like).

What to do:

  1. Read your paragraph out loud. Check it all makes sense to you and think about what is happening.
  2. How can you use your voice to show how the character is feeling? Think about the way you would say the words if it was happening to you in real life!
  3. If your paragraph has speech and narration, think about how to change your voice to show the difference between the character(s) speaking and the narrator.
  4. Read it again two or three times, thinking carefully about how you use your voice to make the meaning clear.
  5. Now it’s getting more familiar, try adding in some facial expressions that would help show how the character is feeling or what they are thinking.
  6. Once you’ve read it a few more times, you might find you don’t need to look at the writing the whole time you are speaking. If you get to this point, you might be able to add in some movements for your character, as if you were an actor on the stage!
  7. Find an audience – it could be someone in your house, on a video call, or you could film yourself – and perform it for them!
